claims.text: Degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 during high-temperature gas exposure is governed by the formation and evolution of surface oxide scales.
Preferential oxidation of Al and Cr under oxidizing conditions produces Al2O3- and Cr2O3-rich scales.
A continuous, compact, and adherent oxide scale limits inward oxygen transport and slows oxidation.
An Al2O3/Cr2O3-rich scale preserves the fcc matrix integrity of the stated alloy.
A 5% H2-in-N2 reducing atmosphere causes incomplete or unstable oxidation of Al and Cr.
Reducing conditions produce non-uniform, porous oxide scales on the stated alloy.
A discontinuous or porous scale permits greater oxygen ingress and internal degradation than a compact scale.
Internal oxygen ingress under reducing conditions leads to spallation and degradation while the fcc structure remains preserved.
The as-built SLM alloy has a stable, single-phase fcc matrix.
The as-built alloy has minimal initial oxide coverage and no preexisting continuous protective scale.
Oxidizing exposure will yield a continuous, adherent oxide scale on the stated alloy.
Oxidizing exposure will produce minimal weight gain or gradual parabolic oxidation kinetics.
Oxidizing exposure will cause limited subsurface damage.
Reducing exposure will cause oxide penetration along grain boundaries.
Reducing exposure will produce a higher overall degradation rate than the starting-state baseline.
Exposure at 800–900 °C for 50–200 hours avoids secondary phase transformations that could disrupt the fcc matrix.
Chromia can form volatile CrO3 above 900 °C.
Alumina formation and the associated Al depletion can destabilize an alloy's structure.
Parallel exposures in 21% O2/N2 and 5% H2/N2, with weight-change measurements and post-exposure microscopy and spectroscopy, can distinguish the proposed environmental mechanisms.
Similar scale morphology, internal oxidation, and weight-change behavior in the two gas environments would falsify the proposed environment-dependent mechanism.

contradictions.description: The reducing condition is specified only as 5% H2 in N2, with no oxygen or oxygen-bearing impurity level stated, yet the mechanism predicts oxide formation, accelerated oxygen ingress, and internal oxidation in that environment.

The hypothesis asserts that Al-rich scale formation preserves fcc matrix integrity, while the cited mechanistic context acknowledges that alumina formation and Al depletion can cause structural instability; the hypothesis does not resolve this competing effect.
